```{ojs}

K = Object.fromEntries(K0.map(d => [d.key, d.value]))
```

```{ojs}
md`<div class="cs-lead">Staff per student at public colleges <b>fell or held flat from 2000 to 2012, then rose</b>. From FY2013 to FY2024 the typical surviving college added <b>${f1(K.ratio_rise_unw)}</b> log points of staff per student (${f1(K.ratio_rise_w)} counting every employee and student together). Most of that is the denominator: enrollment fell ${f1(-K.fte_dlog_unw)} points while staff fell ${f1(-K.staff_dlog_unw)}.</div>`
```

::: {.cs-links}
Read more: [white paper §4](../paper/index.qmd#sec-4) (staffing since 2012) and [§9](../paper/index.qmd#sec-9) (conclusions). Substack post: Post 4 (link on publication).
:::

```{ojs}
md`### Four findings

<div class="cs-kpis">
<div class="cs-kpi"><div class="v">${f1(K.split_enrollment)} + ${f1(K.split_beyond)}</div><div class="l"><b>Why staff per student rose.</b> Of a ${f1(K.split_rise)}-point rise (1,903 colleges with the population instrument), ${f1(K.split_enrollment)} points come from staffing that moves less than one for one with enrollment, ${f1(K.split_beyond)} from staff growth beyond enrollment</div></div>
<div class="cs-kpi"><div class="v">${f1(K.dec_dlog_fte)}</div><div class="l"><b>Enrollment fell, mostly not from population.</b> Change in log fall FTE FY2013–24 = population ${s1(K.dec_demographic)}, business cycle ${s1(K.dec_cycle_national)}, everything else ${s1(K.dec_residual)}</div></div>
<div class="cs-kpi"><div class="v">${f2(K.elas_pr)} / ${f2(K.elas_rp)} / ${f2(K.elas_cc)}</div><div class="l"><b>Staffing elasticity</b> to population-driven enrollment: public research / regional publics / community colleges. Below 1 in every public sector</div></div>
<div class="cs-kpi"><div class="v">${f0(K.enrf_share_of_rise)}%</div><div class="l"><b>Hiring to attract students.</b> Enrollment-facing staff (student affairs, counseling, athletics, media, sales) rose ${f1(K.enrf_dlog)} log points FY2015–24, about ${f0(K.enrf_share_of_rise)}% of the rise in staff per 1,000 students</div></div>
</div>

<div class="cs-kpis">

<div class="cs-kpi"><div class="v">${f1(K.dual_cc_2013)}% → ${f1(K.dual_cc_2023)}%</div><div class="l">of community-college FTE that is high-school dual enrollment, fall 2013 → 2023; CC FTE ${f1(K.cc_fte_incl)} log points with it, ${f1(K.cc_fte_excl)} without (FY2014–24)</div></div>
```

## By sector

```{ojs}
viewof sx = Inputs.radio(new Map([["Staff per 1,000", "pk"], ["FT faculty per 1,000", "ftf"], ["Enrollment", "fte"]]), {value: param("k", "pk"), label: "Show"})
```

```{ojs}
{
  setParam("k", sx === "pk" ? null : sx);
  const SG = {pr: "pr", pm: "rp", pb: "rp", cc: "cc", xr: "xr", xm: "xmb", xb: "xmb"};
  const el = k => EL.find(d => d.sg === SG[k] && d.base === "b1987" && d.outcome === "total");
  return html`<div class="cs-scroll"><table class="cs-sectab"><thead><tr><th>Sector</th>
    <th>Staff per 1,000<br>FY2000</th><th>FY2012</th><th>FY2024</th><th>FT faculty per 1,000<br>FY2012 → 24</th><th>Fall FTE<br>FY2012–24</th><th>Staffing elasticity<br>(sector group)</th></tr></thead><tbody>
    ${SECTORS.map(s => { const e = el(s.k); return html`<tr><td><span class="sw" style="background:${s.c}"></span>${s.l}</td>
      <td>${f0(K[`pk_${s.k}_2000`])}</td><td>${f0(K[`pk_${s.k}_2012`])}</td><td><b>${f0(K[`pk_${s.k}_2024`])}</b></td>
      <td>${f1(K[`ftf_${s.k}_2012`])} → ${f1(K[`ftf_${s.k}_2024`])}</td><td>${s0(K[`fte_${s.k}_12_24`])}%</td>
      <td>${e ? `${f2(e.coef)} (${f2(e.se)})` : "–"}</td></tr>`; })}</tbody></table></div>`;
}
```

```{ojs}
{
  const m = sx === "pk" ? "total" : sx === "ftf" ? "ftfac" : null;
  if (!m) {
    return html`<p class="cs-note">Enrollment trends by sector and peer group are on the <a href="../enrollment/index.html">Enrollment</a> page.</p>`;
  }
  const pts = TR.filter(d => d.m === m && d.fy >= 1990).map(d => ({...d, lab: SECL[d.sec]}));
  const dom = [d3.min(pts, d => d.unw) * 0.95, d3.max(pts, d => d.unw) * 1.03];
  const ends = spreadLabels(SECTORS.map(s => { const l = pts.filter(d => d.sec === s.k).at(-1); return {x: l.fy, y: l.unw, label: `${s.l} ${f0(l.unw)}`}; }), {domain: dom, height: 340});
  return Plot.plot({
    width: Math.min(width, 900), height: 340, marginRight: width < 600 ? 10 : 150, marginLeft: 44,
    x: {...yearAxis}, y: {grid: true, domain: dom, label: `${MEASL[m]} per 1,000 FTE students`},
    color: {domain: SECTORS.map(s => s.l), range: SECTORS.map(s => s.c), legend: width < 600},
    marks: [Plot.rectX([{a: 1989.5, b: 2012.5}], {x1: "a", x2: "b", fill: SHADE}),
      Plot.lineY(pts, {x: "fy", y: "unw", stroke: "lab", strokeWidth: 2}),
      width < 600 ? null : Plot.text(ends, {x: "x", y: "ly", text: "label", dx: 6, textAnchor: "start", fontSize: 10, fill: INK}),
      Plot.tip(pts, Plot.pointer({x: "fy", y: "unw", title: d => `${d.lab}, FY${d.fy}: ${f1(d.unw)}`}))]
  });
}
```

::: {.cs-note}
Staff per 1,000 fall FTE students, S24 surviving set (1,909 institutions), mean of institution ratios; shaded years are those covered by the 2014 Delta Cost brief. FT faculty per 1,000 rose in every sector from FY2012 to FY2024. Enrollment change: sector totals, S24. Elasticity: two-stage least squares of total staff on fall FTE using the gravity population instrument (standard error in parentheses); public master's and bachelor's colleges are pooled as regional publics, private master's and bachelor's colleges are pooled. Private-sector first stages are weak. Every number on this page is listed with its source file and column in [kpis.csv](../data/kpis.csv). Data: IPEDS (FY2024–25 NCES provisional), Census and SEER population, BLS LAUS, EADA.
:::
